subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: What framework-level plugin circuit breaker contract should OpenClaw support for plugin hooks/tools, storage, operator controls, and default degradation behavior?
rationale: Current main has hook timeouts and plugin-local breaker precedent, but choosing fail modes, forced-open behavior, status/reset surfaces, storage schema, and default-on policy changes the plugin runtime and third-party plugin contract.

options.title: Design core breaker contract first
options.body: Define the generic hook/tool breaker API, SQLite state schema, status/reset surfaces, default compatibility mode, and per-plugin degradation policy before implementation.

options.title: Limit to plugin-owned breakers
options.body: Keep breakers in individual plugins like Active Memory and add only narrow SDK helpers if multiple plugins need the same mechanism.

options.title: Start with passive telemetry
options.body: Add attribution and log-only evaluation first, then decide active open/half-open behavior after deployment data.

recommendation.title: Design core breaker contract first
recommendation.body: Define the generic hook/tool breaker API, SQLite state schema, status/reset surfaces, default compatibility mode, and per-plugin degradation policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal for the hook/tool/lock surfaces is vincentkoc's recent agent-core/plugin-runtime refactor and hook contract work.
